claims.text: An APPEND-ONLY, HASH-CHAINED JSONL file per council at runs/council/<council_id>.jsonl.
claims.why: DEFAULT_COUNCIL_DIR = ROOT / 'runs' / 'council' and council_store_path builds <council_id>.jsonl; append-only is enforced by later functions not in this chunk but the file location claim is established.

claims.text: every line carries the SHA of the line before it
claims.why: _entry_sha(prev, body_sha, ts) hashes prev with \0 separators; genesis prev None folds to '' as documented.

claims.text: so a flipped byte or a deleted INTERIOR line breaks the chain and verify_chain NAMES the offending 1-indexed line
claims.why: verify_chain is not in this chunk; the naming behavior cannot be observed here.

claims.text: TAIL truncation (any prefix of a valid chain is itself a valid chain) is caught only against the head/count ANCHOR persisted beside the transcript and re-checked on every verify.
claims.why: anchor_path exists but anchor writing and verify_chain are outside this chunk.

claims.text: It deliberately REIMPLEMENTS memstore.py's two-SHA discipline instead of importing it, and it must never write to the memory ledger.
claims.why: The file defines its own _body_sha and _entry_sha and _resolve_store refuses paths under _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR.

claims.text: Any store path under <repo>/memory/ is refused loudly by _resolve_store.
claims.why: _resolve_store resolves the path and raises ValueError if it is relative to _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR.

claims.text: body_sha -- sha256 over json.dumps(canonical_body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=True) where canonical_body is the record MINUS the four position/identity fields ts, prev, entry_sha, id (and body_sha itself).
claims.why: canonical_body excludes _NON_BODY_FIELDS which is exactly {'ts','prev','entry_sha','id','body_sha'}; canonical_body_json uses those exact json.dumps args; _body_sha hashes the utf-8 bytes.

claims.text: entry_sha -- sha256(prev + "\0" + body_sha + "\0" + ts), the chain link. Genesis prev is None and folds in as "".
claims.why: _entry_sha builds payload = (prev or '') + '\0' + body_sha + '\0' + ts and hashes it.

claims.text: a turn's id is entry_sha[:16], not body_sha[:16]
claims.why: id assignment is in append_turn, not in this chunk.

claims.text: there is NO dedupe
claims.why: Dedupe logic would be in append_turn; not visible here.

claims.text: append_round takes a whole round's turns in ANY completion order, sorts them by the vendor-namespaced actor id, assigns seq at chain time, and stamps ONE chain timestamp for the round.
claims.why: append_round is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Real per-turn wall-clock lives in meta.latency_ms / meta.started_ts, which are body content, not chain position.
claims.why: meta keys are allowed in _ALLOWED_META_KEYS but the claim about chain position requires append_turn.

claims.text: PATH channel: every evidence path, INDIVIDUALLY.
claims.why: _scan_paths iterates over paths and calls secret_floor_rule(str(p), '') one at a time.

claims.text: CONTENT channel: the turn content, every ref, and every metadata string, each scanned on its own -- never over the assembled turn.
claims.why: _scan_texts exists and scans one string at a time, but _scan_turn's full composition is not visible.

claims.text: A hit REFUSES the turn -- no redact-and-send, no redact-and-store.
claims.why: The refusal behavior is in _scan_turn or append_turn; not visible here.

claims.text: In its place a status="refused" receipt is chained naming ONLY the rule label (a fixed string, never matched text)
claims.why: Receipt construction is in append_turn, not in this chunk.

claims.text: The receipt is re-scanned before it is written; if the identity fields themselves carry the secret the receipt degrades to an anonymous one
claims.why: Re-scan and anonymous degradation are in append_turn; not visible here.

claims.text: withheld (paths an egress lane declined to send) is scanned with the CONTENT channel only, never the path channel.
claims.why: The scan composition is in _scan_turn; not visible here.

claims.text: EVERY REQUESTED PARTICIPANT PRODUCES EXACTLY ONE CHAINED TURN PER ROUND -- content, refused, unavailable with a machine reason, or budget_exhausted. Silence is never an absence.
claims.why: This is enforced by append_round/append_turn; not visible here.

claims.text: A turn is one of these and nothing else. There is deliberately no "ok" here
claims.why: TURN_STATUS tuple contains exactly spoke, refused, unavailable, budget_exhausted, anomaly; no 'ok'.

claims.text: Machine reasons -- fixed vocabulary
claims.why: UNAVAILABLE_REASONS and ANOMALY_REASONS are literal tuples of fixed strings.

claims.text: Fail-closed ceiling on a single turn. Transcript tokens grow as O(V^2 R^2), not O(V R); the per-council budget lives in session.py, but no single turn may blow the file up on its own.
claims.why: MAX_CONTENT_CHARS is defined as 200_000 but its enforcement is in append_turn; the session.py budget is external.

claims.text: ADR-010 actor-namespace rule, pinned to the MODEL and not just the vendor
claims.why: _ACTOR_RE matches 'council.<vendor>.<model>' with vendor and model parts; actor_id builds exactly that.

claims.text: A key outside this set is REFUSED loudly, never dropped: a silently dropped field lets two semantically distinct turns canonicalise to the same body
claims.why: The refusal logic is in append_turn or _scan_turn; not visible here.

claims.text: Per-store append index: tail entry_sha + record/turn counts, keyed by resolved path and invalidated by the file's (size, mtime_ns). Re-parsing the whole transcript per append is O(n^2) overall; a 500-turn council must not pay that.
claims.why: _APPEND_CACHE is defined but its population and invalidation are in append functions not in this chunk.

claims.text: The content projection body_sha is taken over: everything EXCEPT the position/identity fields. Uniform across turn and roster records so the chain walk needs no per-record-type branch.
claims.why: canonical_body filters out _NON_BODY_FIELDS; the uniform behaviour is exactly that filter.

claims.text: The exact bytes hashed. Exposed so a test can assert determinism against the canonical form rather than against a digest it cannot inspect.
claims.why: canonical_body_json returns json.dumps(...) with deterministic args; it is the exact input to _body_sha.

claims.text: ``council.<vendor>.<model>`` per ADR-010. An unknown model id is recorded as the literal ``unknown`` by the CALLER -- never omitted, never inferred.
claims.why: actor_id returns exactly f'council.{vendor}.{model}'; the caller-handling part is a statement about callers, not contradicted here.

claims.text: One evidence citation: the path as given plus the sha256 of the exact bytes shown to the model. Two participants citing "the file" may have been shown different bytes; without this the transcript records a citation that cannot be reproduced.
claims.why: evidence_ref returns {'path': str(path).replace('\\','/'), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()}.

claims.text: ``<base_dir>/<council_id>.jsonl``. ``council_id`` is filename-safe by validation, not by sanitising: a silently rewritten id would point two councils at one transcript.
claims.why: council_store_path calls _check_council_id, which raises on invalid ids, then joins with f'{council_id}.jsonl'.

claims.text: The head/count anchor beside the transcript. Separate file on purpose: the chain walk cannot detect tail truncation from a truncated file alone.
claims.why: anchor_path returns p.with_name(p.name + '.anchor.json'), a separate file.

claims.text: Resolve and REFUSE any path under <repo>/memory/.
claims.why: _resolve_store resolves the path and raises ValueError if it is under _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR.

claims.text: PATH channel, one path at a time -- so a hit is attributable to one path and a diff that ADDS .env cannot hide inside a blob.
claims.why: _scan_paths loops over each path and calls secret_floor_rule(str(p), '') individually.

claims.text: CONTENT channel, one string at a time. ``path=""`` here is correct and is NOT the forbidden whole-prompt call: the path tier is run separately over every evidence path above, so it is never skipped.
claims.why: _scan_texts calls secret_floor_rule('', str(t)) per string; the path tier is separate in _scan_paths.

observations.what: The module docstring makes many behavioral claims about append_round, verify_chain, and secret floor refusal that are not verifiable in this chunk; they are all UNCHECKABLE.

_resolve_store returns the unresolved path (p) on success, not the resolved path; the resolved path is only used for the forbidden check. This could cause ambiguity if base_dir is a symlink, but the claim only says refuse under memory.
The chunk defines _ACTOR_RE but nothing in this chunk uses it; its enforcement is in later functions.
The comment above _ALLOWED_TURN_KEYS says a key outside the set is REFUSED loudly, but the refusal logic is not in this chunk; it is uncheckable here.
